messages:
lee: DAST nightly is bombing in integration env. Error from the scanner when uploading evidence to GCS: access denied on CMEK-encrypted bucket. Anyone familiar with the recent CMEK hardening?
ci-bot: job=ci/dast-run id=834 failed. Excerpt:
```
Failed to upload report: storage.Error: googleapi: Error 403: The caller does not have permission
Caused by: failed to decrypt object key using CMEK projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/dast/cryptoKeys/dast-cmek-key: PERMISSION_DENIED
```
rija: We rolled forward CMEK key policy last week to constrain decrypt rights to the `cloudrun-instances@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` principal only. DAST runs as ephemeral GH Actions runners that impersonate `gha-actions@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
maria: That sounds like the mismatch. Why wasn't the CI preflight caught? We added a checklist but maybe not for CMEK on buckets.
dev: Quick repro: impersonated the GH Actions SA and attempted a decrypt: 
```
$ gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=dast --key=dast-cmek-key --ciphertext-file=ct.bin --plaintext-file=- --impersonate-service-account=gha-actions@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
ERROR: (gcloud.kms.decrypt) PERMISSION_DENIED: Member gha-actions@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com does not have permission to use the CryptoKey
```
oncall: Short mitigation options: 1) add gha-actions SA to CryptoKeyDecrypter for that key (key-level binding) and re-run pipelines; 2) temporarily switch the bucket to Google-managed key (no CMEK) while we patch infra; 3) update DAST runner to use Workload Identity or Cloud Run service that has decrypt permissions. Recommend option 1 for fastest restore.
rija: I can push a scoped binding for just the bucket/key with a short TTL. Will coordinate with ops.
ci-bot: re-triggered ci/dast-run id=835 (triggered by rija).
ci-bot: Status: failed -> still getting storage 403 when scanner tries final upload.
lee: Logs show the scanner process uses `gsutil cp` which fails at the storage layer because the object is encrypted with CMEK and the upload completes but finalization attempts decrypt? (odd). Anyone know the exact flow for CMEK with uploads?
maria: When uploading with CMEK the storage service writes the object encrypted with the provided CMEK; the KMS Decrypt call is needed for multipart compose or rewriting existing objects. If uploader lacks decrypt on the key, certain operations will fail.
dev: Workaround applied: rija added the key binding for gha-actions SA (roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter) scoped to the key. Also added `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on the bucket for that SA.
ci-bot: Retrying ci/dast-run id=836.
ci-bot: Status: succeeded (dast id=836).
lee: Good. Root cause: policy scoping tightened to run-level principal but we missed GH Actions identity. Follow-ups: we need preflight checks for CMEK-affecting changes and better mapping of principals that rely on buckets (DAST, SCA scanners, compliance exports).
oncall: Create paging rule: if any service reports CMEK PERMISSION_DENIED > 3 in 10m for a CI principal, page oncall + eng-infra.
sec-bot: Playbook: https://wiki.internal/redwood/sec/sdlc/cmek-hardening-playbook. Post-incident checklist added: 1) inventory buckets using this key, 2) map principals that access them, 3) run ephemeral-runner impersonation smoke tests before rollouts.
maria: I'll file SECURITY-802 "CMEK preflight + runner identity audit" and include a script that enumerates bucket->principal mappings and runs an impersonated decrypt smoke test for each principal.
rija: Also propose: update scanner infra to proxy uploads through a Cloud Run uploader service that has a stable SA with decrypt rights (reduces the number of principals we must grant CMEK to).
dev: Agree. That moves blast radius to a single service account we control and audit. We'll prototype this in sandbox.
lee: Thanks all. I'll add notes to the SDLC checklist and close once SECURITY-802 is created and the short-lived key binding is expired (rija pls set TTL).
